# About this document

This file contains the R code used to create the six figures included in the data story. It contains code and explanatory comments only; the figures themselves appear in the `data_story.pdf`.

Figures produced by this code:

- Figure 1: Filled line chart — national fatality trend
- Figure 2: Calendar heatmap — year by month pattern
- Figure 3: Slope chart — state comparison 1989 vs 2021
- Figure 4: Stacked bar chart — time slot and crash type
- Figure 5: Lollipop chart — road user totals
- Figure 6: Diverging bar chart — age group and gender

---

# Setup

## Packages

```{r packages}
# Data
library(dplyr)     # for filtering, grouping, summarising
library(tidyr)
library(readr)     # for reading the CSV file
library(forcats)

# Charts
library(ggplot2)   # all six figures are built with ggplot2
library(scales)    # for comma() to format numbers on axes
library(ggrepel)   # for non-overlapping labels in slope chart
```

## Colour palette

```{r colours}
# These four colours are used across all six figures.
# Red  = primary highlight colour
# Blue = comparison group or context

INK  <- "#1F1F1F"   # for text and labels
GREY <- "#777777"   # for axis text and secondary labels
RED  <- "#B5533C"   # main accent colour
BLUE <- "#3A6EA8"   # comparison colour
```

## Shared ggplot theme

```{r theme}

theme_story <- function(base = 11) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base) +
    theme(
      plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#EEEEEE",
                                         linewidth = 0.4),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text          = element_text(colour = GREY, size = 9),
      axis.title         = element_blank(),
      plot.caption       = element_blank(),
      legend.position    = "top",
      legend.title       = element_blank(),
      legend.text        = element_text(size = 9, colour = INK),
      plot.margin        = margin(4, 4, 2, 4)
    )
}
```

## Load and clean data

```{r load-data}
# Read the dataset.
crash <- read_csv("Crash_Data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r clean-data}
# Convert columns that came in as text to numeric.
crash <- crash |>
  mutate(
    Age   = as.numeric(Age),
    Year  = as.numeric(Year),
    Month = as.numeric(Month)
  )

# Set factor order for Day of week and Time of day.

crash <- crash |>
  mutate(
    `Day of week` = fct_relevel(`Day of week`, "Weekday", "Weekend"),
    `Time of day` = fct_relevel(`Time of day`, "Day", "Night")
  )

# For figures that use gender, drop the one record where gender is listed as Unspecified.
crash_g <- crash |>
  filter(Gender %in% c("Male", "Female"))
```

---

# Figure 1 — Filled line chart

```{r fig1}
# Count total fatalities for each year.
yearly <- crash |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# The line emphasises the year-to-year change in fatalities.
# Two annotations mark the start and end values so the reader

fig1 <- ggplot(yearly, aes(x = Year, y = n)) +
  geom_area(fill = RED, alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line(colour = RED, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(colour = RED, size = 1.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Label the opening value
  annotate("text", x = 1990, y = 2780,
           label = "2,800 deaths (1989)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = INK) +
  # Label the closing value in the accent colour
  annotate("text", x = 2020.5, y = 720,
           label = "843 deaths (2021)",
           hjust = 1, size = 3, colour = RED, fontface = "bold") +
  # Dotted lines to mark two major policy periods
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1997, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 1997.5, y = 2920, hjust = 0,
           size = 2.5, colour = GREY,
           label = "RBT & seatbelt\nenforcement") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2011, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = GREY, linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 2011.5, y = 2920, hjust = 0,
           size = 2.5, colour = GREY,
           label = "National Road\nSafety Strategy") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, limits = c(0, 3200),
                     breaks = seq(0, 3000, 500)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1990, 2020, 5)) +
  theme_story()
```

---

# Figure 2 — Calendar heatmap

```{r fig2}
# Filtered to 2000 onwards because the chart would be very tall
ym <- crash |>
  filter(Year >= 2000) |>
  group_by(Year, Month) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Colour goes from pale (few deaths) to dark red (many deaths).
# This shows both the long-term improvement (rows get paler)
# and the seasonal pattern (January tends to be darker).

fig2 <- ggplot(ym, aes(x = Month, y = Year, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FDF0EC", high = RED,
                      name = "Deaths/month") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb,
                     position = "top", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(2000, 2020, 5),
                  expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 9, colour = INK),
    legend.position  = "right",
    legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
    legend.title     = element_text(size = 8)
  )
```

---

# Figure 3 — Slope chart

```{r fig3}
# fatality count for each state in 1989 and 2021 only.

state_slope <- crash |>
  group_by(State, Year) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(Year %in% c(1989, 2021))


# States with less than 60% decline are coloured red.
# These are the slow-progress states the story focuses on.
pct_tbl <- state_slope |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = n,
              names_prefix = "y") |>
  mutate(
    pct  = (y2021 - y1989) / y1989 * 100, # Calculate percentage change per state.
    slow = pct > -60
  )

state_slope <- left_join(state_slope,
                          select(pct_tbl, State, slow),
                          by = "State")


left_labs  <- filter(state_slope, Year == 1989)
right_labs <- filter(state_slope, Year == 2021) |>
  left_join(select(pct_tbl, State, pct), by = "State") |>
  mutate(lab = paste0(State, "  ", round(pct), "%"))

# ggrepel is used for both sets of labels so they do not overlap.
fig3 <- ggplot(state_slope,
               aes(x = factor(Year), y = n,
                   group = State, colour = slow)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = left_labs, aes(label = State),
                  hjust = 1, nudge_x = -0.1, size = 3,
                  show.legend = FALSE, direction = "y",
                  segment.colour = "grey80",
                  segment.size = 0.3) +
  geom_text_repel(data = right_labs, aes(label = lab),
                  hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.1, size = 3,
                  show.legend = FALSE, direction = "y",
                  segment.colour = "grey80",
                  segment.size = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = RED, "FALSE" = BLUE),
    labels = c("TRUE"  = "Slower progress (< 60% decline)",
               "FALSE" = "Faster progress (> 60% decline)")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 1.5)) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 11, colour = INK,
                                    face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

# Figure 4 — Stacked bar chart

```{r fig4}
# Group fatalities by day of week, time of day, and crash type.
tod_dow <- crash |>
  group_by(`Day of week`, `Time of day`, `Crash Type`) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    slot = fct_relevel(
      paste(`Day of week`, `Time of day`),
      "Weekday Day", "Weekday Night",
      "Weekend Day", "Weekend Night"
    )
  )

# Red = single vehicle, Blue = multiple vehicle.
# White labels inside each bar show exact counts so the reader

fig4 <- ggplot(tod_dow,
               aes(x = slot, y = n, fill = `Crash Type`)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(n)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            colour = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Single" = RED, "Multiple" = BLUE),
    labels = c("Single"   = "Single-vehicle crash",
               "Multiple" = "Multi-vehicle crash")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "Weekday Day"   = "Weekday\nDay",
    "Weekday Night" = "Weekday\nNight",
    "Weekend Day"   = "Weekend\nDay",
    "Weekend Night" = "Weekend\nNight"
  )) +
  theme_story()
```

---

# Figure 5 — Lollipop chart

```{r fig5}
# Count total fatalities per road user type.
# Arranged from lowest to highest so the chart reads

road_totals <- crash |>
  filter(`Road User` %in% c("Driver", "Passenger", "Pedestrian",
                             "Motorcycle rider", "Pedal cyclist")) |>
  group_by(`Road User`) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(n) |>
  mutate(`Road User` = factor(`Road User`, levels = `Road User`))

# A lollipop chart has a stem (segment) and a dot (point).

# The count is printed inside each dot.

fig5 <- ggplot(road_totals, aes(x = n, y = `Road User`)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = n, yend = `Road User`),
               colour = "#CCCCCC", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 12, colour = RED) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(n)),
            colour = "white", size = 2.8, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#EEEEEE",
                                       linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

# Figure 6 — Diverging bar chart

```{r fig6}
# Age group labels for the legend
age_labs <- c("0_to_16"     = "0-16",
              "17_to_25"    = "17-25",
              "26_to_39"    = "26-39",
              "40_to_64"    = "40-64",
              "65_to_74"    = "65-74",
              "75_or_older" = "75+")

# red for the young groups,
# blue for middle age, lighter shades for older groups.
age_cols <- c("0_to_16"     = "#E8D5CF",
              "17_to_25"    = RED,
              "26_to_39"    = "#C97A61",
              "40_to_64"    = BLUE,
              "65_to_74"    = "#7AA3C4",
              "75_or_older" = "#B8CCE0")


# Female counts are made negative so they plot to the left of zero.

# Male counts stay positive and plot to the right.
arg <- crash |>
  filter(
    Gender     %in% c("Male", "Female"),
    `Road User` %in% c("Driver", "Passenger", "Pedestrian",
                        "Motorcycle rider", "Pedal cyclist"),
    `Age Group` %in% c("0_to_16", "17_to_25", "26_to_39",
                        "40_to_64", "65_to_74", "75_or_older")
  ) |>
  group_by(`Age Group`, `Road User`, Gender) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    plot_val    = ifelse(Gender == "Female", -n, n),
    `Road User` = fct_relevel(`Road User`,
                   "Pedal cyclist", "Motorcycle rider",
                   "Pedestrian", "Passenger", "Driver"),
    `Age Group` = fct_relevel(`Age Group`,
                   "0_to_16", "17_to_25", "26_to_39",
                   "40_to_64", "65_to_74", "75_or_older")
  )

# The diverging bar puts female on the left and male on the right.
# The x axis labels show absolute values on both sides so the
# reader reads them as counts, not negative numbers.


fig6 <- ggplot(arg,
               aes(x = plot_val, y = `Road User`,
                   fill = `Age Group`)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = -10000, y = 5.65,
           label = "<-- Female", colour = GREY,
           size = 3, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 10000, y = 5.65,
           label = "Male -->", colour = GREY, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) comma(abs(x)),
    breaks = c(-15000, -10000, -5000, 0,
                5000,  10000,  15000, 20000),
    limits = c(-20000, 20000)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = age_cols, labels = age_labs) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
